description: CSIRO publishes measurements of faecal indicators and opportunistic pathogens in roof-harvested rainwater tanks in southeast Queensland, Australia. The named CSIRO collection shows one public file and CC BY 4.0. Its Open Health Data paper describes 24 tanks sampled at six monthly events from August 2015 to March 2016, yielding 144 samples. The Excel table includes three faecal indicator groups and six opportunistic pathogens measured with culture or qPCR methods. Drinking-water or household rainwater modellers can use these observations to calibrate microbial exposure and test whether seasonal variation changes a quantitative risk assessment. The measurements cover a small regional set of tanks, so they do not establish contamination rates for all Australian rainwater systems. The paper abstract gives a conflicting “March 2006” end date, while its coverage and methods sections give 2016; the latter is used here. The spreadsheet was not downloaded, and pathogen concentrations and assay limits were not independently checked. The catalogued Freshwater Watch record is a related but different water-quality observation source.
name: Survey of faecal indicators and opportunistic pathogens in rainwater tank samples
